final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and largely reframed the same record. Their narrowing is directionally correct: aggregate readiness and the absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support launch-readiness context, while the current refund-workflow regression is a material weakness for a named launch use case. But that narrowed position is still not enough for compliant_with_caveats on this record. The distinction is that a caveated conclusion would require admissible evidence that the required caveat is actually present in the current release documentation or that an approved mitigation/risk acceptance exists. Here, the policy text makes disclosure or approved mitigation a compliance predicate, and the record still lacks evidence of either. Because the unresolved concern is not merely overbroad wording but an unevidenced policy condition, certification remains suspicious rather than compliant_with_caveats.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows that the current release documentation or certification record actually reflects the current evaluation batch and explicitly discloses the refund-workflow regression.
The policy makes disclosure or approved mitigation a condition for certification when a named launch use case has a material weakness; that predicate remains unmet in the record.
No approved risk acceptance, reviewed mitigation, or owner acceptance is evidenced.
Prior approval and informal monitoring remain contextual only and cannot satisfy the current-release certification requirement.
